_arch_note: ARM C — the confidence gate with "bounded"'s full selectivity and a corrected scale: confidence_form="bounded" with confidence_gain=12.61. Config cloned verbatim from sweep_s05_dout48_H4_tph256_c256_din32/config.json; the ONLY deltas are lut_forward_confidence=true, lut_confidence_form="bounded", lut_confidence_gain=12.61 and the seed. The gain was chosen by measurement, not guessed: on 6,291,456 real margin vectors at this sizing, bounded scores 0.05423589 mean and bounded_norm 0.68383604, a ratio of 12.6086, so gain 12.61 puts bounded's mean at 0.683915 — within 0.011% of arm A''s. That makes C vs A' a ONE-VARIABLE comparison isolating SELECTIVITY: identical forward scale, but p75/p25 2.06 vs 1.09 and within-token CV 0.536 vs 0.061. Arm A (bounded, no gain) and arm A' (bounded_norm) each moved two variables at once and so cannot separate "the scale was wrong" from "the selectivity is useless". The gain is a constant, hence exactly absorbable into the linear decompress, so it adds no parameters and no expressive power — the param count is exactly the baseline's and any difference is mechanism rather than capacity. One seed, paired against baseline S5 (1.434572). This is C1, random_seed 1.
